_comment: The keys a language's keyboard strip offers. There is nothing to fill in:
a language folder carries a flag and a name, and between them that is
enough to know which letters to put on the strip.
byName is tried first, on the folder's name with the flag stripped and
lowercased, so 'Español' and 'Spanish' both land on the same row. byCountry
is the fallback, on the flag — which is the more reliable of the two,
because the flag is picked from a list when the language is created while
the name is free text somebody may have written as 'Spanish practice'.
For a language written in the Latin alphabet the strip holds the letters a
US keyboard cannot reach, not the whole alphabet — a b c are already keys.
For every other script there is no such distinction, so those get the
alphabet itself. Space-separated, so an entry can hold a digraph: 'll',
'ch', 'dž' and 'ij' are single letters to the languages that use them.
